title: Multimodal transformer separates diabetic from other renal disease using fundus images
summary: Trans-MUF, a transformer system using fundus images and clinical characteristics, reported an AUC of 0.980 on an internal retrospective set, 0.989 on a prospective dataset and 0.932 on a multicenter, cross-machine, multi-operator dataset for distinguishing diabetic nephropathy from non-diabetic renal disease. Nephrologist accuracy rose by 21% with visualization assistance. Cohort sizes and the reference standard are not in the abstract, and the very narrow confidence intervals suggest image-level analysis; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: Transformer-based multimodal deep learning system (Trans-MUF) on fundus images and clinical characteristics
organization: Chinese PLA General Hospital; Chinese People's Liberation Army; State Key Laboratory of Kidney Diseases

evidence.tested: Internal retrospective set, a prospective dataset and a multicenter cross-machine dataset; classified as retrospective or benchmark because prospective freezing and the reference standard are not documented.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes, biopsy reference, patient-level analysis and clinical benefit; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Distinguishes diabetic nephropathy from non-diabetic renal disease to avoid unnecessary biopsy.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
